subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Dana,

Great to meet you and Oliver on the call earlier — thanks for the time and the demo walkthrough. As discussed, I wanted to summarize next steps for a Hosted API evaluation and share the quickstart resources so your engineers can get a test integration going today.

Recap / recommended path for evaluation:
- Start with Hosted API (fastest to spin up, zero infra) to validate call patterns and latency on a realistic request mix.
- If you need strict data residency or a committed throughput SLA later, we can discuss Dedicated capacity or Private VPC — I included a short comparison below.

Quickstart links (attached): redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (setup + sample requests) and a Postman collection (attached) with example requests. Key details:
- Base endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Auth: API key in Authorization: Bearer <key> header
- Common params: model, max_tokens, temperature, stream=true/false

Rate limits (Hosted API initial tier - for evaluation):
- Default: 60 requests/minute and 200k tokens/minute per account
- Burst policy: short bursts up to 120 req/min achievable for 1-2 minutes depending on queue
- If you need higher sustained throughput we can request a temporary lift for the eval or discuss Dedicated capacity (see below).

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (high level):
- Hosted API: best for fast evaluation and early production use; managed by Redwood, shared pools, predictable token pricing.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for a single customer; predictable throughput & lower per-token cost at scale; monthly commit and SLA.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network and control plane, required for regulated data residency/air-gapped needs; longer lead time and licensing.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll provision a temporary eval API key for Acme and attach the quickstart.
2) Your infra/engineering team runs a smoke test (sample Postman collection) and shares 1-2 sample prompts and expected TPS.
3) We reconvene next week to review latency metrics and discuss capacity (if you need higher throughput or data residency).

Let me know if you prefer a quick pairing session with Dev or Rishi for the integration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf, acme-eval-postman-collection.json

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple quick questions from our side after the call:

1) Data residency: our platform stores and processes some PII and financial metadata; for the Hosted API evaluation, will Redwood retain logs or prompt data? We need to understand retention and whether requests are processed in a shared multi-tenant pool.

2) Rate limits: the default you shared should be fine for a simple spike test, but if we want to simulate a sustained 500 TPS (for a core realtime use case) what is the recommended path? Dedicated capacity only?

3) Timeline & cost: roughly how long to provision Dedicated vs Private? We’re early in evaluation but want to map procurement steps.

Happy to jump on another short call — Oliver and I can make time tomorrow afternoon PST if that helps.

—Dana

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Dana — great questions, answered inline below.

Data residency / retention:
- Hosted API evaluation: request & response data are processed in Redwood’s multi-tenant serving fleet. By default, we retain request logs and raw prompts for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; that retention can be adjusted for enterprise customers.
- If you need zero retention or on-prem processing, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the path we recommend. For Dedicated we can offer strict contract terms (and reduced retention windows) and ensure traffic is restricted to your reserved pool.

Rate limits & 500 TPS scenario:
- Sustained 500 TPS (~tokens/min depends on request size) is outside typical Hosted tiers. Options:
  - Temporary eval lift: we can provision a short-term quota increase for the evaluation (subject to approvals) to simulate higher TPS for a day or two.
  - Dedicated capacity: recommended for sustained high throughput. Dedicated gives you a predictable GPU pool and higher per-account concurrent request capacity; provisioning typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on availability and contract.

Timeline & cost high-level:
- Hosted API: immediate (minutes) — pay-as-you-go.
- Dedicated: procurement + infra lead time — generally 2-6 weeks depending on contract complexity and region. Pricing is monthly committed capacity (we’ll share SKUs after we size your expected sustained throughput).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): longer lead time (4-12+ weeks) and licensing/ops fee; used for strict compliance or air-gapped environments.

If you’re okay starting with Hosted for functional and latency validation, I’ll:
- Create an eval key (24-72 hour elevated quota window available if you want a short stress test)
- Share a short checklist for performance metrics to capture (p95/p99 latency, error rates, tokens/min)

Would you like Dev or Rishi to join tomorrow’s pairing session to walk your engineers through the Postman collection? We can make someone available at 2pm or 4pm PST.

Best,
Marissa
